extracted text: The paper investigates the effect of Si additions (0.3, 0.6, and 0.9 wt%) on Al-4Cu-1.3Mg alloy. The alloys were homogenized at 490°C for 24h, and subsequently at 520°C for 12h, followed by air cooling to room temperature. The billets were then extruded at 420°C. The plates were solution treated at 500°C for 3h followed by immediate quenching into cold water, and finally aged for different periods of time at 190°C. The peak aging time was determined to be 12h at 190°C, which corresponds to a T6 temper. The microstructure analysis showed that different precipitates formed depending on Si content: S'-Al₂CuMg in the Si-free alloy, S'+σ-Al₅Cu₆Mg₂ in 0.3Si and 0.6Si containing alloys, and S'+β'-Mg₂Si in the 0.9Si containing alloy.
